questions.prompt: ____, I never go swimming right after I eat.
questions.explanation: “As a rule” means normally or as a general habit. It introduces the speaker’s usual practice.

questions.prompt: He was ____ for words when he won the award.
questions.explanation: “At a loss for words” means unable to think of what to say, often because of surprise or strong emotion.

questions.prompt: How did you ____ such a clever idea for a story?
questions.explanation: “Come up with” means think of or create an idea. Use the base form after “did.”

questions.prompt: She was the perfect choice ____ finding someone to organize the conference.
questions.explanation: “When it came to” means regarding the matter of something. The past tense matches “was.”

questions.prompt: There was no need to ____ the mistake. Everyone could see it.
questions.explanation: “Point out” means indicate or draw attention to something. The mistake was already obvious.

questions.prompt: He drank ____ because he was driving.
questions.explanation: “Neither A nor B” excludes both choices. He drank no beer and no wine because he was driving.

questions.prompt: We ____ an old friend of ours at the movie theater.
questions.explanation: “Ran into” means met by chance. They unexpectedly met an old friend.

questions.prompt: You could ____ your grandparents for information about your ancestors.
questions.explanation: “Look to A for B” means turn to someone to provide something. The grandparents may provide family information.

questions.prompt: ____ the terrible weather, we had a nice time on our vacation.
questions.explanation: “In spite of” means despite. They enjoyed the vacation even though the weather was bad.

questions.prompt: Although our team name is the Buccaneers, people call us the Bucs ____.
questions.explanation: “For short” introduces a shortened version of a name. “Bucs” is shorter than “Buccaneers.”

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.explanation: Alice unexpectedly met someone earlier that day.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Robert Smith, the boy who used to cut our lawn.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I ____. What does he look like?
lines.explanation: Tom cannot think of or remember the person Alice is describing.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Remember? He had blonde hair and glasses. He was really short.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Nope. I'm not ____ any kid like that in my memory.
lines.explanation: Tom is not able to think of a child who fits that description.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Anyway, he's starting college. Now he has ____ glasses. He has dark hair and he's much taller.
lines.explanation: Robert no longer has either of the two identifying features: blonde hair or glasses.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: But ____ the fact that he is grown up, he still chews bubble gum!
lines.explanation: He still chews bubble gum despite being grown up.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Now I remember him! We used to call him Bob ____.
lines.explanation: “Bob” is a shortened form of Robert’s name.

story.title: Idioms in context
paragraphs: My husband and I went to a high school reunion party in our old town. Almost one hundred people were there. As a rule, I enjoy meeting people. But when it comes to large, noisy parties, I get very tired. I told my husband that I would prefer not to stay for too long. My husband pointed out that we should at least say hello to the people that we knew. We did run into several old friends at the party, so in spite of the crowd I still had a good time.
During the party, a young man came up to us. “Hello, Mr. and Mrs. Brown,” he said to us.

He looked familiar, but I didn’t know where I had seen the young man before. I knew it was no use looking to my husband for help. He is terrible at coming up with names to match with faces. This time, we were both at a loss to think of his name. We talked with the young man for a while and then a couple came up to us. It was Don and Liz Wilson. (Her name is Elizabeth, but everyone calls her Liz for short). They were friends of ours. We had kept in touch, but had not seen them for many years.

The young man left after a few minutes to talk with some of his other friends. I told the Wilsons, “I’m sorry we did not introduce you to that nice young man. Neither my husband nor I could figure out his name.” “That’s all right,” said Mr. Wilson, “He is our son.”
